title: Exceptional Virtual Assistant for Airbnb Business - 8AM - 4PM PST
description:
Day Shift Operations Coordinator

**Vo Rental ("Vo Place Like Home") — Anaheim, CA**



About us



Vo Rental owns and manages a portfolio of roughly 50 short-term rental and residential properties. The core of the business is in Orange County — Anaheim, Garden Grove, Westminster, Santa Ana, Midway City — with additional homes in Las Vegas, Panama City and Panama City Beach, FL, and Kissimmee, FL. We run a cleaning team of about 19 people and turn over homes every single day of the year.



This is an operations job, not a desk job. Guests check out at 11 AM and the next guests walk in at 4 PM. Everything we do lives inside that window.



The role



You are the person who owns the turnover day. From the first checkout message to the last house cleared, you keep guests informed, cleaners moving, and every turnover finished on time. You work alongside our night-shift coordinator, who hands you the day and picks it back up when you sign off.



Schedule and pay



- **Hours:** 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM PST (Pacific Standard Time, US West Coast)

- **Days:** Tuesday through Sunday. Mondays off.

- **Pay:** $1,200 per month



What you'll do



**Turnover and cleaner coordination**



- Monitor guest messages and confirm when guests have actually vacated each home

- Notify the assigned cleaner the moment her house is clear

- Build and balance the daily cleaning assignments across the team; reassign when someone calls out, a booking extends, or a house gets added late

- Send each cleaner her next-day schedule and any special instructions (guest counts, supply drops, promised early check-in times)

- Track that every checkout has a cleaner assigned and every clean is finished before check-in



**Guest communication**



- Answer guest questions on Airbnb, 
, and direct channels — access codes, parking, early check-in and late checkout requests, local recommendations

- Handle same-day problems: a lockout, a missing item, an AC that isn't cooling, a cleaner running behind

- Keep tone warm and responses fast; most of our reviews are won or lost here



**Damage claims and documentation**



- Collect and organize post-clean photo documentation from cleaners

- Intake damage reports: rename and timestamp photos, gather receipts, and assemble the supporting file

- Maintain the claims tracker and prepare claims for filing with Airbnb / 



**Maintenance and supplies**



- Dispatch and follow up on repairs, pest control, jacuzzi service, air filter changes, water heater flushes

- Track consumables per property and get restocks to the right house before the next cleaning

- Confirm work was actually completed, not just scheduled



**Records and reporting**



- Log cleaner hours and cleaning fees for monthly payouts

- Support month-end owner and tenant statements

- Keep the task list, calendars, and property records accurate — other people depend on them being right



What we're looking for



**Required**



- Fluent written and spoken English

- Genuinely reliable with time. This job is built on deadlines that cannot slip.

- Strong written communication — clear, short, warm messages to guests and to staff.

- Comfortable running your own day across many small moving pieces without being chased.

- Working knowledge of Google Calendar, Google Sheets or Excel, WhatsApp, and a shared task manager. You should be able to learn a property management system quickly.

- Discretion. You will see guest information, addresses, access codes, and payment records.



**Nice to have**



- Spanish. Much of our cleaning team communicates in Spanish, so it helps every day.

- Prior short-term rental, property management, hospitality, or dispatch experience

- Familiarity with Airbnb and 
 host tools

- Experience coordinating field staff or contractors



**Not required**



- A college degree

- Prior experience with our specific software



What success looks like



- **First 30 days:** You know the properties by name, you know which cleaner covers what, and you can run a turnover cycle start to finish with occasional help.

- **First 60 days:** Guests get answers within minutes. Cleaners hear from you before they have to ask. Nothing on the calendar surprises you.

- **First 90 days:** You catch problems before I do — the booking that extended, the house with no cleaner, the guest who is unhappy but hasn't said so yet.



To apply



**You must include a Loom video or a YouTube clip with your application. I will not entertain any proposal or applicant that does not include one.**



In your video, introduce yourself and tell us about a time you had to fix a scheduling problem in real time — what went wrong, what you did, and how it turned out. Also confirm that you can work 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM PST, Tuesday through Sunday.



You must spend at least 10 AP on this application, or it will not be reviewed.

title: Guest Communications & Marketing Specialist
description:
About us 



Luxury Mountain Destinations manages approximately 150 vacation homes in Park City, Utah — ski-in/ski-out properties in Deer Valley, homes near Park City Mountain, and a growing summer business built on hiking, biking, and the Utah backcountry. 



We're in the middle of a deliberate shift: moving more of our bookings away from the online travel sites and onto our own website. About half our business comes direct today. We want it to be sixty percent. 



We are building a small, senior offshore team — not a call center seat. You will be one of two people we're hiring in the Philippines this year. You and your counterpart will share the guest communications and reservations desk between you on staggered shifts, and each of you brings a second discipline to the team. Yours is marketing. 



This is a genuine two-sided role. Half your week is guests and reservations. The other half is marketing. Both halves matter and we staff, schedule, and measure them separately. 



 



An unusual note about experience 



You do not need vacation rental experience. We will teach you that half of the job. 



Guest communications and reservations are learnable, and we would rather train someone sharp, well-educated, and genuinely good with people than hire someone who already knows a different company's way of doing things. We have a structured six-to-eight week training program and we expect to use all of it. 



What we cannot teach is a real marketing foundation, exceptional English written and spoken, and composure with a demanding guest. Bring those and we'll handle the rest. 



 



What you'll do 



Guest communications and reservations — 50% of your time 



Voice (roughly half of this half). You'll take inbound reservation calls through our phone system. Someone calls asking about a five-bedroom home over Presidents' Week — you find out what they actually need, walk them through the right properties, quote it, and book it. You'll also take service calls from guests already in a home. 



Online. Inquiries and messages by
, text, and through online websites (eg Airbnb). Pre-arrival questions: arrival instructions, ski storage, parking, altitude tips, restaurant recommendations. In-stay issues — triage, enter tickets for and/or route to our Park City operations and maintenance team, follow up until the guest confirms it's resolved. Post-stay follow-up. 



Reservations administration. Modifications, cancellations, ancillary sales, date changes, and payment processing in our property management system and change requests in 3rd party systems (eg Airbnb). 



Reason-coding. Every inquiry that doesn't book gets a reason — price, dates unavailable, wrong property type, no hot tub, too far from the lift. Every time. This is one of the most valuable things you'll do and almost nobody in our industry does it. 



Marketing — 40% of your time 



Note: this role does not manage social media. That sits elsewhere. Your marketing work is direct-booking and owner acquisition demand, content, and lifecycle — the things that move guests from the travel sites onto our own site and bring them back – and the things that compel property owners to complete an introductory call with our Business Development team. 



Guest marketing 



Lifecycle
. Write and schedule campaigns in our CRM — shoulder-season pushes, repeat-guest offers, peak-week announcements, win-back sequences. Build and maintain the segments behind them. 



Property listing content. Write and maintain descriptions, amenity detail, and photo captions on our direct website. Our listings should be the best-written ones a guest sees that day, and there are 150 of them. 



Destination content and SEO. Local guides, seasonal landing pages, on-page SEO. Someone searching "Deer Valley ski-in rental" should find us. 



Direct-booking conversion. Landing pages, promotions and packages, booking-flow copy, and the offers that make booking direct obviously better than booking through an OTA. 



Owner marketing 



Owner communications. Newsletters, market updates, seasonal outlooks, and program announcements to the homeowners whose properties we manage. These are how an owner decides we're an asset manager rather than a booking agent. 



Owner acquisition. Nurture campaigns to prospective homeowners, realtor and broker referral outreach, and the market-report content that gets a second-home owner to call us instead of a competitor. 



Paid media 



Google Ads. Build, run, and optimize search campaigns against a monthly budget. Report on cost per booking, not clicks. 



Meta ads. Paid
 and Instagram campaigns for guest demand and owner acquisition, including audience building and creative iteration. 



Direct mail. Postcard and print campaigns to guest and owner lists — list segmentation, copy, coordination with the print vendor, and tracking what came back. 



 



Property onboarding 



When a new home joins the portfolio, you launch it: write the listing, coordinate photography needs, get it live and consistent across our site and every channel, and run the announcement campaign that gets it booked in its first season. A new property that sits unbooked for two months is a very unhappy owner. 



Reputation and reporting 



Reputation. Respond to public reviews across channels in our brand voice, and flag patterns worth fixing operationally. 



Reporting. Campaign performance, ad spend and return, direct vs. OTA mix, inquiry-to-booking conversion, owner-lead volume. Tell us what's working and what to stop doing. 



 



The advantage you have over any marketer we could hire separately is that you're on the phone and in the inbox every day. You'll hear what guests actually ask, in their own words, before you write a single subject line — and you'll know what they asked for that we don't have. 



Making it better — 10% 



Turn the questions guests ask most into templates, FAQ content, and listing improvements. Cover your teammate's desk during their time off and peak weeks — you are each other's backup. 



 



What we're looking for you to bring 



Education 



Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Advertising, Journalism, Multimedia Arts, English, or Business Administration. This is the one hard credential requirement. 



Certifications in Google Analytics or Google Ads are a plus but not required. 



Experience 



2+ years in marketing, content, copywriting, or communications. Enough that campaign work, a CMS, and a reporting dashboard are familiar territory rather than concepts from a textbook. 



Language — this is the highest bar in the posting 



Excellent spoken English with a clear, neutral, easily understood accent. You will be on the phone with American guests spending thousands of dollars a week. We assess this on a live call. 



Exceptional written English. Not "good" — exceptional. You'll write copy representing a luxury brand and messages that resolve problems for demanding guests. Writing samples required. 



Foundation 



A portfolio: campaigns, listings, landing pages, articles, or long-form writing you actually wrote. 



Hands-on with an
 platform and a CMS. 



Comfort with numbers — you can read a campaign report or a booking pace report and say something useful about it. 



SEO fundamentals: keywords, on-page structure, why a page ranks or doesn't. 



Disposition 



Composure. When a guest is upset at 8 PM about a cold hot tub, you stay calm and useful. 



Coachability. We are going to teach you an industry. You need to take feedback well and get better fast. 



Curiosity about a place you've never been. This matters more than it sounds like it does. 



Self-directed. We don't use time-tracking software and we don't micromanage. We need someone who doesn't require either. 



Setup 



Wired internet, 25 Mbps down / 10 Mbps up minimum, with a backup connection. 



A quiet, enclosed room — this is a voice role and background noise is disqualifying. 



A UPS or backup power plan for storm season (June–November). 



A quality headset. We'll reimburse it. 



A real plus, though not required 



Vacation rental, short-term rental, hotel, resort, or travel/hospitality marketing experience. If you've written listings, run a hotel's
 program, or marketed a destination, say so prominently. 



Vacation rental software: Streamline, Guesty, Hostaway, OwnerRez, Track, Hospitable. 



BPO or call center experience on a U.S. voice account. 



Basic design in Canva. 



Comfort with AI tools — we use them daily and expect you to. We'll also expect you to know when the output sounds like AI and to fix it. 



 



Schedule 



This role works U.S. Mountain Time hours. Park City is 14–15 hours behind the Philippines, so your working day will fall outside standard Philippine business hours — overnight or early morning, depending on the shift. A shift differential applies. 



We staff this desk with two people on staggered shifts, so that between them we cover our full guest day and our busiest check-in days have two people on. Which shift and which days you take depends on the pair we hire and on how demand moves through the year, and schedules can change with reasonable notice. Expect some weekend coverage. We confirm your exact hours and days before you start. 



The U.S. observes daylight saving time and the Philippines does not, so the Mountain Time equivalent shifts by one hour in March and November. We adjust the Philippine-time schedule so your hours stay consistent. 



 



Compensation 



$1,200 USD per month. 



13th month pay. 



15 days (3 weeks) paid time off per year, plus Philippine regular holidays. 



$25 monthly internet and power allowance. 



Headset reimbursement. 



Shift differential. 



Performance bonus tied to direct-booking conversion. And/or owners that progress to sales call 



Annual performance and salary review. 



We pay on time, every time, and we're looking for someone who wants this to be a career, not a stopover. 



 



What's hard about this job 



The guests are wealthy and their expectations are high. When something goes wrong at 8 PM in a $4M house, you're the first person they talk to, and "I'll look into it" is not an answer they accept gracefully. 



Park City is a place you've probably never been. You'll need to learn a mountain town's geography, seasons, and rhythms well enough to advise someone on where to stay and what to do — from the Philippines. If that sounds tedious rather than interesting, this isn't your role. 



And the job asks you to switch between two modes: the interrupt-driven phone and inbox, and focused creative work. We protect the second on your calendar, but you have to be someone who can make that switch cleanly. 



 



How to apply 



Start your application with the word POWDER so we know you read this. 



Send us: 



A short note (under 300 words): your marketing education and background, and where you've dealt with customers, clients, or the public directly. 



Your resume, plus 2–3 writing samples. 



A 60–90 second voice recording introducing yourself and describing a place you love, as if you were recommending it to someone who's never been. Any format. This is required — we assess spoken English early because it's the hardest thing to teach. 



Write a 150-word description for a five-bedroom ski-in/ski-out home in Deer Valley with a private hot tub, a bunk room, and a view of Bald Mountain. Make us want to book it. 



Applications missing the keyword, the voice recording, or #4 will not be reviewed. 



Process: short screening call → work sample (campaign subject lines, a review response, two written guest messages, and a mock reservation call after we give you a property fact sheet) → final video interview with our leadership team. 



Luxury Mountain Destinations is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on demonstrated ability.

title: Ongoing Shopify Developer (Frontend + Backend) — Part-Time, Long-Term
description:
**Project Overview**



We are looking for an experienced Shopify developer to work with us on an ongoing basis, handling both frontend and backend work on our live store.



The store is already built and launched. **This is not a redesign project and not a basic setup job.** What we need is a reliable long-term partner who can handle continuous refinements, feature requests, bug fixes, and backend work as they come up.



You will be our go-to developer for anything the store needs, week to week.



**Scope of Work**



*Ongoing frontend work*

- Design and layout refinements across the store (homepage, product pages, collections)

- Building custom sections and components beyond theme defaults

- Advanced Liquid, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript customization

- Mobile-first fixes and responsive issues

- Bug fixes, broken links, layout inconsistencies

- Small UX improvements and micro-interactions as requested



*Ongoing backend work*

- Shopify Admin API and GraphQL work

- Custom app development and maintenance

- Webhooks, automation, and internal tooling

- Third-party app integration, configuration, and troubleshooting

- Data handling: product, inventory, and order workflows

- Multi-channel sync work (Shopify + Etsy / eBay / Amazon) as needed



*Continuous optimization*

- Page speed and Core Web Vitals

- SEO best practices and structured data

- Code cleanup and performance tuning

- Analytics and tracking maintenance (GA4, Meta Pixel)



**Requirements**



- 5+ years of professional Shopify experience (non-negotiable)

- Strong portfolio of live Shopify stores you have built or maintained

- Advanced Shopify Liquid, HTML, CSS, JavaScript

- Solid backend ability: Shopify Admin API / GraphQL, custom app development, webhooks, and at least one backend language (Node.js or Python preferred)

- Comfortable working across both frontend and backend without hand-offs

- Good UI/UX judgment — you should be able to implement a request well, not just literally

- Experience with page speed optimization, SEO, and structured data

- Able to work independently with minimal supervision

- Strong, responsive communication in English



Applications without a strong Shopify portfolio will not be considered.



**Bonus (Highly Preferred)**



- Jewelry or luxury e-commerce experience

- Graphic design skills (banners, promotional creatives)

- Multi-channel integration experience

- CRO and A/B testing experience



**Working Arrangement**



- **10–20 hours per week**, ongoing

- **Hourly rate**, billed through tracked time logs

- Time tracking is required, with a short note on what each block of hours covered

- Weekly progress summary

- Requests come in continuously — we need someone available and responsive during the week, not batching everything into one day

- Store access will be granted on a least-privilege basis, scoped to what the work requires

- Code must be clean, documented, and maintainable — no shortcut or throwaway solutions



We are looking for a long-term professional partner, not a one-off freelancer. If this works well, the hours and scope can grow.



**To Apply**



Please include:

1. Links to Shopify stores you have worked on, and what specifically you did on each

2. An example of backend or custom app work you have done on Shopify

3. Your hourly rate and typical weekly availability

4. Your timezone and usual working hours

title: Executive Assistant
description:
Executive Assistant

About BBG

BBG (formerly Bermuda Bulk Gases and Tools & Equipment Unlimited) supplies industrial and medical gases, hydraulic hose assemblies and industrial products throughout Bermuda.

We’re building on a long history while investing in the future. Under new leadership, we’re strengthening our people, systems and technology to build an organisation designed to become stronger over time.



The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to work closely with the Executive and become an important part of how their work gets done.

Your role is to help the Executive use their time and attention more effectively. You’ll provide administrative support across both business and personal matters, helping organise their time, information, communication and commitments.

You’ll work closely with the Executive and Chief of Staff, take responsibility for important details and continually look for ways to make the Executive more effective.



What You’ll Do

You’ll help the Executive use their time and attention effectively by:

Managing their calendar, scheduling, travel and other logistics.

Managing correspondence and helping prepare and draft communications.

Organising business and personal administrative matters.

Keeping track of commitments, requests and follow-ups.

Preparing, reviewing and organising documents and information.

Anticipating needs and handling routine matters without unnecessary involvement from the Executive.

Supporting the Chief of Staff with administrative execution.

As you develop your understanding of the Executive and the organisation, you’ll increasingly recognise what requires the Executive’s attention, what can be handled independently and how to make the best use of their time.



Who We’re Looking For

You have strong character. You’re trustworthy, discreet and understand the responsibility that comes with having access to confidential business and personal information.

You’re exceptionally dependable and organised. You follow through on commitments, communicate when plans change and make sure important details don’t get dropped.

You’re proactive and exercise judgement. You anticipate needs, recognise what you can handle independently and know when something requires the Executive’s attention.

You communicate clearly and professionally and make information easy for others to understand and act on.

You have a love of learning. You ask questions, learn from experience and continually look for ways to become more effective.

You’re comfortable using technology and AI to improve the way you work.



Technical Foundation

You should have:

Experience supporting a busy executive or business owner.

Excellent written and spoken English.

Strong organisational and administrative skills.

Experience using modern productivity software.

The following experience is highly desirable:

Managing complex calendars, travel and executive logistics.

Drafting correspondence and working with confidential information.

Working in a remote or distributed team.

Using AI and automation to improve the way you work.



Compensation & Benefits

Competitive compensation.

Ongoing training and development.

Opportunities for increased responsibility and career progression.

The opportunity to build a long-term career with BBG.



Hiring Process

Our hiring process is designed to help both you and BBG confirm whether we’re likely to be a strong long-term fit.

The process will include an application, online assessment, short video response, interviews and a practical assessment.

title: Online Fitness Coaching Assistant (Everfit)
description:
About us

SR FitWell is a personal training business in Perth, Western Australia, run by Scott Richmond out of Snap Fitness Yanchep. We coach around 30 clients, a mix of in-person and online. Most are everyday people, not athletes. Shift workers, mine workers, mums, blokes in their forties getting back into it.



We are small and we intend to stay personal. Every client is known by name. That matters for this role, because you will get to know them too.



We are in Perth, which is the same timezone as the Philippines. No overnight shifts, no working while we sleep. When you are online, we are online.

The role

Scott handles the in-person coaching. What he does not have time to do properly is the online side, and that is where you come in.



You will own the weekly rhythm of our online coaching inside Everfit. Reading what clients have logged, updating their programs, keeping their nutrition targets current, and flagging anyone who is drifting before they disappear.



This is not general admin. You need to genuinely understand training and nutrition, because you will be looking at a client's week and d
 what needs to change.



You will not be inventing our method. We have written it all down. Our programming rules, our nutrition approach and our client templates are documented and you will be trained on them. Your job is to apply that system consistently, week in and week out, and to tell Scott when something needs his judgement.



What you will do each week



Review every active client's Everfit dashboard and note who is on track and who is not

Read the weekly check-in forms clients submit each Saturday and summarise what matters

Update and progress workout programs in Everfit in line with our documented method

Keep macro and nutrition targets current as clients' weight and goals change

Assign the next block of workouts before a client's current program runs out

Flag anyone who has gone quiet, missed sessions, or stalled, so Scott can call them

Keep client folders and records tidy and up to date

Prepare a short weekly summary for Scott every Sunday morning so he knows where everyone is at

Escalate anything involving injury, illness, pregnancy, medication or anything outside our normal system straight to Scott, never handle it yourself

What we need from you

Solid working knowledge of resistance training. You should know what progressive overload is, why rest periods matter, and how to structure a training week without being walked through it

A genuine understanding of macros and calories. You should be comfortable with protein targets per kilogram of bodyweight and be able to spot when a number looks wrong

Excellent written English. You will be reading what clients write about their week and summarising it accurately for Scott

Reliable. This is a weekly rhythm and it has to happen every week without being chased

Comfortable saying "I am not sure, can you check this" rather than guessing. We would much rather that

Stable internet and a computer that can run Everfit in a browser without trouble



Nice to have, but we will train you

Experience with Everfit specifically. If you have used Trainerize, TrueCoach, PT Distinction or similar, that transfers fine

A fitness qualification of any kind

Experience working with Australian or other English speaking clients

Canva

Hours and schedule

Around 10 to 15 hours per week to start, spread across the week however suits you, with two fixed commitments:



Saturday evening or Sunday early morning to review check-ins as they come in

Sunday morning to have the weekly summary ready for Scott



There is genuine scope to grow this into full time as we take on more online clients.



HOW TO APPLY

Please do not send a generic application. We read every one properly and we can tell.



Send us:



Put the word BARBELL at the start of your subject line so we know you read this properly

A short note about your experience with fitness coaching or training, and which coaching platforms you have used

Answer this question in two or three sentences: A client has trained all four of their sessions every week for a month, they are logging their food accurately, and their weight has not moved at all. What are the first three things you would check?

Tell us your internet speed and whether you have a backup if it drops out



We will reply to everyone who follows the above. Shortlisted applicants will be asked to do a short-paid test task using a real anonymized client example, then a video call with Scott

title: Freelance Content Marketer & Content Creator
description:
We’re looking for a freelance content marketer and content creator with strong editorial judgment, audience awareness, and the ability to turn business goals into useful, engaging content.



This is a flexible, project-based GIG. We will start with a small number of assignments—about 5–10 hours per week depending on workload. If we find a strong fit, there is potential for regular ongoing work and more projects, but this is not a full-time role at present.



The work is centered on content marketing: understanding the audience, finding strong content angles, creating high-quality content, adapting it across channels, and improving it based on results. We do not want keyword-stuffed or bulk-generated content.



TYPICAL PROJECTS



• Research audiences, customer problems, competitors, topics, and relevant trends.

• Turn business goals and audience needs into useful content ideas, briefs, outlines, and small campaigns.

• Write and edit blog posts, landing pages, guides, newsletters, case studies, campaign copy, and other marketing content.

• Turn one strong idea into multiple formats for social media,
, and other channels.

• Maintain a clear, consistent brand voice while adapting tone and format for different audiences and platforms.

• Fact-check claims and use reliable sources.

• Review content performance and suggest practical improvements.

• Apply sensible on-page SEO where relevant, including search intent, headings, internal links, metadata, and natural topic coverage.

• Structure content clearly so it can also be understood and cited by AI-powered search and answer engines.

• Deliver polished work on time and communicate progress clearly.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR



• A portfolio of polished, published English-language content.

• Demonstrable experience in content marketing, content creation, copywriting, or editorial work.

• Strong storytelling, structure, tone, clarity, and attention to detail.

• Ability to understand an audience and create content that is useful, original, and aligned with a business goal.

• Ability to develop an idea—not simply rewrite or summarize existing articles.

• Ability to adapt content for long-form, social media,
, and other formats.

• Strong research, fact-checking, editing, and source-evaluation skills.

• Good organization, communication, and reliability in a remote working environment.

• Responsible use of AI tools, with human judgment, verification, and substantial editing.

• A practical understanding of SEO is helpful. Experience with GEO or AI search optimization is a plus.



NICE TO HAVE



• Experience with WordPress or another CMS.

• Familiarity with analytics, Google Search Console, GA4, Ahrefs, Semrush, or similar tools.

• Experience creating content briefs, editorial calendars, content series, or topic clusters.

• Experience measuring engagement, traffic, leads, conversions, or other content outcomes.

• Experience with social media content,
 marketing, or conversion copywriting.



HOW TO APPLY



Begin your application with the words “Clear Content” so we know you read the full post.



Please include:



1. A short introduction explaining why this gig fits you.

2. Links to three relevant English-language content samples. Include at least one long-form piece and one social media or campaign example, and state exactly what you contributed.

3. One example of content you created that supported a business goal or improved engagement, traffic, leads, conversions, or another result. Include context and numbers where available.

4. Your concise answers to the screening questions below.

5. Your weekly availability and expected hourly rate.



SCREENING QUESTIONS



1. Choose one sample from your portfolio. Who was the audience, what was the business goal, and why did you choose that angle and format?

2. If you were given one strong topic idea, how would you turn it into a small content campaign across long-form content and two other channels?

3. What makes a piece of content genuinely useful—not merely well written?

4. How do you research and fact-check a topic you do not already know?

5. How do you use AI tools while keeping content accurate, original, and human?



Please do not send a generic application. We value concise, specific answers.



Shortlisted candidates may be invited to complete a short PAID, non-production content test. The fee will be agreed in advance, and the test material will not be published or used commercially.

title: Graphic Designer
description:
Job Description: Graphic Designer 



About the Role 



We are looking for a talented Graphic Designer to join our creative team and support the design needs of a growing digital marketing and web agency. This role is ideal for someone who understands the fundamentals of strong visual design, brand consistency, layout, typography, color theory, and digital-first creative production. 



The right candidate should be comfortable creating professional design assets for websites, social media, paid advertising, branding,
 campaigns, and occasional print materials. We value designers who can think creatively, follow brand guidelines, adapt to different client industries, and produce high-quality work without relying heavily on AI-generated design. 



AI tools may be used as part of a modern workflow, but this role requires a designer with real design judgment, strong fundamentals, and hands-on experience using professional creative software. 



Responsibilities 



Create high-quality visual assets for websites, landing pages, social media, paid ads,
 campaigns, presentations, and print materials. 



Design graphics for Meta ads, Google display ads, organic social media content, website banners, blog images, thumbnails, flyers, brochures, and brand collateral. 



Support brand identity development, including logos, color palettes, typography selections, brand guidelines, and visual systems. 



Edit, resize, and adapt creative assets for multiple platforms and formats. 



Work with marketing, web development, and content teams to create visuals that align with campaign goals and client brand standards. 



Prepare production-ready files for both digital and print use. 



Maintain organized design files and follow internal naming, storage, and version-control practices. 



Review creative briefs and translate business goals into visually effective design concepts. 



Ensure all creative work is consistent, polished, and aligned with each client’s brand voice and audience. 



Make revisions based on feedback while maintaining strong design quality and attention to detail. 



Stay current with design trends, digital advertising formats, social media creative standards, and modern design tools. 



Required Qualifications 



Proven experience as a Graphic Designer, Visual Designer, Brand Designer, or similar creative role. 

Strong portfolio showing professional design work across digital marketing, branding, websites, social media, and advertising. 

Strong understanding of design fundamentals, including layout, hierarchy, typography, color, composition, spacing, and brand consistency. 



Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, especially: 

Adobe Photoshop 

Adobe Illustrator 

Adobe InDesign 

Adobe XD or Adobe Express is a plus 

Ability to create and edit original design assets, not just modify templates. 



Experience designing for digital marketing campaigns, including Meta/Facebook ads, Instagram graphics, Google display ads, and website imagery. 



Ability to follow brand guidelines and adapt design style across multiple client brands. 



Strong attention to detail and ability to produce polished, client-ready work. 



Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced agency environment. 



Good communication skills and ability to accept feedback professionally. 



Preferred Qualifications 



Experience working in a digital marketing agency, web agency, or creative agency. 

Canva experience for creating editable client-facing templates. 

Experience with Figma, Sketch, or other modern UI/design collaboration tools. 

Basic understanding of website design principles, responsive layouts, and UX/UI best practices. 

Experience creating brand identity packages, social media ad campaigns, and landing page graphics. 

Experience preparing files for print production. 

Basic understanding of motion graphics, video editing, or animation is a plus. 

Familiarity with tools such as Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, or similar platforms is a plus.

title: Mobile/Web UX/UI Designer (StoryChat)
description:
Mobile/Web UX/UI Designer (StoryChat)





We run StoryChat (storychat.app) — an AI roleplay and character-chat platform where creators publish characters and stories, and earn from the people who chat with them. Think "YouTube for AI roleplay." Our users are mostly young adults in the US. We're a small, fast-moving team based in Seoul, and we're about to launch our iOS and Android apps.



Our category is crowded and moving fast: Character.AI, Janitor AI, Talkie, Chub, SpicyChat, Polybuzz, Linky, and a dozen more. Some of them have better UX than we do. Your job is to know exactly why, and close the gap.



What this role really is



This is not a "make it pretty" role. We need a designer who thinks like a product person: someone who studies competitors obsessively, argues about what not to build, tests designs on real users, and then checks that what shipped actually matches the design.



Four things you'll own:



1. Competitor teardowns and specs



Regularly audit competitor apps (Character.AI, Janitor AI, Talkie, SpicyChat, Chub, Polybuzz, and new entrants) on both mobile and web.

Document their flows screen by screen: onboarding, character discovery/search, chat UI, memory and persona settings, image generation, creator/character-creation tools, monetization and paywalls, moderation and content filters.

Produce short, decision-ready teardowns: what they do, why it works, what it costs to copy, and what we should do differently. Screens + annotations, not essays.

Maintain a living reference library of competitor patterns we can pull from.



2. Mobile and web product design



Design end-to-end flows for our React Native (Expo) mobile apps and our web app.

Work in Figma with a consistent component library, iOS/Android platform conventions, dark mode, and real edge cases (empty states, errors, loading, long text, offline).

Design for a chat-first product: message bubbles, streaming responses, typing/thinking states, regenerate, edit, memory, long-scroll performance, and mobile keyboard behavior.



3. Feature curation and prioritization



Help d
 which features make the cut. Our competitors ship a lot; we ship the right things.

Turn vague ideas into clear specs with acceptance criteria, or push back with evidence when a feature isn't worth it.

Simplify existing screens. Cutting things counts as a win here.



4. Design QA and usability testing



Review every build against the design before release: spacing, type, states, tap targets, animations, edge cases. File clear, reproducible tickets with screenshots and expected vs. actual.

Test on real devices — a range of Android phones and iPhones, small and large screens, plus web breakpoints.

Run lightweight usability tests: recruit 5–8 users (we can help), write the script, moderate the sessions, and report findings ranked by severity with recommended fixes.

Use our analytics (PostHog) to find where users drop off, then design and validate fixes. We'll teach you the tooling; you bring the curiosity.

Basic accessibility checks: contrast, text scaling, screen reader labels on key flows.

Requirements

3+ years designing mobile apps and/or web products — with shipped work you can point to in an app store.

Strong Figma skills: components, variants, auto layout, prototypes, and clean handoff files a developer can build from.

You've done real usability testing before, even informally, and can talk about what you learned from watching users struggle.

You can write. Specs, teardowns, and bug reports are a big part of this job, and they need to be clear in English.

Comfortable with consumer apps aimed at young adults — social, entertainment, gaming, or creator-economy products.

You use AI chat products yourself and have opinions about them.

Reliable communication, and 4+ hours of daily overlap with Korea time (only 1 hour ahead of Manila).



Nice to have



You've used Character.AI, Janitor AI, or similar apps as an actual user.

Familiarity with React Native / Expo constraints, or experience working closely with mobile developers.

Motion and micro-interaction design.

Experience with creator tools, subscriptions, or in-app currency and paywalls.

Illustration, branding, or marketing asset design (a bonus, not the job).



Not required



A design degree.

Coding — though understanding what's expensive to build is a real advantage.

What you'll get

Real ownership of a product with actual users, not mockups in a drawer.

Direct work with the founder. Short feedback loops, no design-by-committee.

Flexible hours and fully remote.

Long-term role with room to grow into a lead design position as we scale.

How to apply



Applications that skip these steps won't be reviewed. Please send:



Your portfolio — link, PDF, or Figma. Highlight 1–2 mobile app projects and tell us what you specifically did.

A short teardown (this is the real test). Pick one of Character.AI, Janitor AI, Talkie, or SpicyChat. In under 300 words plus 2–3 annotated screenshots, tell us:

one thing they do better than StoryChat, and why it works;

one clear UX problem in their app, and how you'd fix it.

One thing you'd change about StoryChat. Sign up at storychat.app, spend ten minutes in it, and tell us the single change you'd make first. Be blunt — we prefer honest over polite.

Your logistics — hours per week you can commit, monthly rate expectation in USD, timezone, and how soon you can start.

Start your message with the word CURATOR so we know you read the whole post.



Shortlisted applicants get a small paid test project (a real screen from our roadmap, roughly 4–6 hours of work) before we make an offer.



We read every complete application and reply either way.

title: Amazon Wholesale Catalog Analyst & Supplier Sourcing VA
description:
SOV Retail Group is looking for an experienced Amazon Wholesale Catalog Analyst & Supplier Sourcing Virtual Assistant.



This is not a basic data-entry position. We need someone who has previously worked with an Amazon Wholesale business, can analyze distributor catalogs, identify viable purchasing opportunities, source legitimate suppliers, and contribute practical experience to improve our operation.



The selected candidate will work directly with the company owners.



CORE RESPONSIBILITIES



1. WHOLESALE CATALOG ANALYSIS



• Clean and organize distributor and manufacturer catalogs.

• Match supplier SKUs, model numbers and UPCs to the correct Amazon ASINs.

• Detect incorrect matches, variations, sizes, bundles and multipack differences.

• Review Keepa price, Buy Box and sales-rank history.

• Evaluate price stability, seller count, competition and Amazon’s presence on the listing.

• Estimate monthly sales and the realistic sales allocation available to our company.

• Calculate referral fees, FBA fees, preparation costs, inbound shipping, net profit, ROI and margin.

• Review minimum order quantities, case packs, availability, MAP and marketplace restrictions.

• Flag products involving hazmat, expiration dates, meltable inventory, oversized dimensions or other operational risks.

• Classify every analyzed product as BUY, TEST, WATCH or REJECT.

• Explain the reasoning behind every recommendation.

• Present the final shortlist in a clear and accurate Google Sheet.



A profitable calculator result alone does not make a product a good opportunity. The analysis must consider price history, demand, competition, seller behavior, Amazon presence, restrictions, inventory risk and all relevant costs.



2. SUPPLIER SOURCING AND ACCOUNT OPENING



• Research legitimate U.S. distributors and manufacturers.

• Verify whether suppliers accept e-commerce and Amazon resellers.

• Identify brands, product categories, territories, minimum orders and account requirements.

• Locate wholesale applications and relevant contacts.

• Complete account applications using approved company information.

• Contact suppliers professionally by
 and telephone.

• Request catalogs, price lists, terms, MAP policies and e-commerce policies.

• Follow up on applications and unanswered communications.

• Record every supplier, contact, response, document, status and next action in our Google Sheets supplier CRM.

• Provide a weekly report showing leads, applications, approvals, rejections, follow-ups, analyzed catalogs and blockers.



REQUIRED EXPERIENCE



• At least one year of experience working with an Amazon Wholesale business.

• Previous experience analyzing wholesale distributor or manufacturer catalogs.

• Practical experience matching UPCs and supplier products to ASINs.

• Ability to interpret Keepa charts, not simply read current values.

• Experience calculating net profit, ROI and profit margin.

• Understanding of Amazon referral fees and FBA fulfillment fees.

• Understanding of SKU, UPC, ASIN, FNSKU, MOQ, case pack, MAP and MSRP.

• Strong Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel skills.

• Strong spoken and written English.

• Experience communicating with U.S. suppliers by
 and telephone.

• Ability to explain why a product should or should not be purchased.

• Strong attention to detail and ability to work independently.



Experience limited to Online Arbitrage or Retail Arbitrage does not qualify as wholesale catalog-analysis experience.



PREFERRED TOOLS



Experience with some of the following is preferred:



• Keepa

• Amazon Seller Central

• SellerAmp

• SmartScout

• InventoryLab

• Sellerboard

• SellerSnap

• Scan Unlimited, Analyzer.Tools or similar bulk catalog-analysis software



SCHEDULE AND COMPENSATION



• Part-time: 20 hours per week.

• Monday through Friday, approximately four hours per day.

• At least two hours of overlap with U.S. Eastern Time business hours.

• Starting compensation: US$7–US$8 per hour based on demonstrated experience.

• Paid practical assessment for finalists.

• Paid two-week trial period.

• Performance and compensation review after 60 days.

• Opportunity for additional hours and responsibilities based on performance.



EXPECTED CONTRIBUTION



We do not want someone who only copies information or depends entirely on automated software.



We want someone who can:



• Explain why a supplier is or is not worth pursuing.

• Identify false-positive products in catalog scans.

• Recognize missing costs and risks before recommending inventory.

• Explain what Keepa is showing and defend a purchasing recommendation.

• Share processes that worked for a previous Amazon Wholesale employer.

• Recommend practical improvements to our supplier and catalog workflow.



HOW TO APPLY



Begin the subject line of your application with:



CATALOG 2026



Applications without this phrase will not be reviewed.



Answer all the following questions:



1. Describe your most recent Amazon Wholesale role and the exact tasks you performed.

2. How many years of Amazon Wholesale experience do you have?

3. Describe the largest wholesale catalog you analyzed and approximately how many products it contained.

4. Explain your process for converting a supplier catalog into a shortlist of potential products.

5. Which tools have you used for catalog analysis?

6. What information do you examine in Keepa before recommending a purchase?

7. How do you match a supplier product to the correct ASIN when the UPC is missing or incorrect?

8. How do you detect a single-unit versus multipack mismatch?

9. Explain the difference between ROI, profit margin and net profit.

10. Describe a product that appeared profitable but that you rejected after completing your analysis.

11. How did you find and qualify distributors for your previous employer?

12. Approximately how many wholesale accounts did you help open?

13. Are you comfortable calling U.S. suppliers in English?

14. What hours can you work in U.S. Eastern Time?

15. Confirm whether you accept US$7–US$8 per hour for 20 hours per week.



Also include:



• A link to a short voice recording introducing yourself and explaining your Amazon Wholesale experience.

• A sanitized example of a wholesale catalog analysis you previously completed, if available. Remove all confidential information.

• A list of the Amazon and catalog-analysis tools you have personally used.



SELECTION PROCESS



Applicants will pass through the following stages:



1. Application and experience review.

2. English voice-recording review.

3. Interview and live Keepa questions.

4. Paid practical catalog-analysis assessment.

5. Paid two-week working trial.



During the paid assessment, finalists will analyze a sample wholesale catalog and provide:



• Correct product and ASIN matches.

• Keepa observations.

• Estimated demand and competition.

• Amazon fees and operating costs.

• Net profit, ROI and margin.

title: Wanted: Designer Clothing Supplier / Sourcing Agent - Bulk, Ongoing Monthly Orders
description:
We are an established vintage, secondhand and designer clothing retailer in Australia with physical stores and a large online presence. We are looking for reliable suppliers or sourcing agents who can source authentic secondhand designer clothing in bulk, every month, as a long-term arrangement.



What we buy



Authentic secondhand pieces from designer and luxury brands, including (but not limited to):



Japanese designer and streetwear: Comme des Garçons (incl. Homme, Play, Shirt), Junya Watanabe, Issey Miyake (incl. Pleats Please, Homme Plissé), Yohji Yamamoto, Y-3, Needles, Hysteric Glamour, Kapital, BAPE, Cav Empt, Evisu

European and international designer: Burberry, Vivienne Westwood, Yves Saint Laurent, Christian Dior, Gucci, Prada, Miu Miu, Balenciaga, Versace, Dolce & Gabbana, Moschino, Hermès, Fendi, Givenchy, Celine, Valentino, Salvatore Ferragamo, Bally, Armani (Emporio, Armani Jeans), Maison Margiela, MM6, Stone Island, C.P. You source items and send us clear photos of each piece: front, back, and all tags (brand, size, fabric/care labels), along with your price per item.

title: Performance Video Editor (High Salary)
description:
Performance Video Editor

Exchange Life · Fully Remote · Full-Time Contractor · ~40 hrs/week $10–20 USD/hour depending on experience + uncapped performance bonuses



About Exchange Life

Exchange Life is one of the fastest-growing e-commerce travel jewellery brands in the US. We sell collectible country charms for traveller's, with new products launching soon. Our content machine has generated over a quarter billion views across TikTok and Instagram.



This role is video, end to end. You'll concept and cut short-form video ads for paid media across TikTok, Reels, and Meta placements, where every edit is judged on what it does to hook rate, retention, and spend. You're not making brand films or organic filler. You're making the creative we put budget behind.



We're looking for an editor who can own their output and be creative within proven marketing fundamentals, not just execute tasks. This is not a gig; it's a long-term partnership. Many of our editors have been with us 2+ years, and the people who now set our creative direction started as editors here.



You'll work closely with our Content Lead and Marketing team. We're a small, high-output team that moves fast, communicates daily, and invests in the people who show up.



Where You'll Be in Six Months

Senior Performance Video Editor.



That's the next title, and it's within reach inside your first six months if your work earns it. At that level you have full creative autonomy: you own video concepts end to end, you d
 which angles we test next instead of receiving briefs, your creatives are the ones we put real spend behind, and you start reviewing other editors' cuts and shaping how they work.



It's d
 by performance, not time served. Move faster if your work moves faster.



Compensation & Earning Potential

Base: $10–20 USD/hour depending on experience

Performance bonuses: Uncapped, paid per winning creative. Every video that hits our performance thresholds or scales on paid ads pays out.

Rate reviews: Revisited as you take on more, not on an annual calendar

Our top editors earn meaningfully more than their base because they produce winners consistently. That's the whole design: we'd rather pay a lot for creatives that work than a little for creatives that don't.



What Success Looks Like

After 3–6 months, a successful hire is consistently producing short-form video ads that scale on paid and perform organically, hitting 50%+ thumb-stop rates and 30%+ hold rates, and iterating on winning formats without needing direction from the marketing team. You'll be a trusted creative partner, not just an executor.



Core Responsibilities

Concept and edit short-form video ads for TikTok, Reels, and Meta, built around hook rate, retention, and watch time rather than aesthetics

Develop new video angles and hooks, then test them against our proven formats

Build AI-assisted video creative using current tools, and keep pace as those tools change

Review your past edits daily, identify what's working and what isn't, and improve without repeating mistakes

Work directly from paid performance data to d
 what to cut next

Turn around content quickly and communicate proactively every day, with no check-ins required

Stay on top of TikTok and Instagram trends and apply them where they'll actually convert

Must-Haves

A strong recent portfolio of short-form video edits, ideally including paid ad creative (20+ from the last few months)

You can watch a winning video ad and break down exactly what made it work

Hands-on experience across video formats: hook-led headline videos, talking heads, voiceovers, UGC-style edits, AI video

Ability to read metrics (hook rate, retention, watch time, spend) and know what to change in the next cut

Takes ownership, internalizes feedback, doesn't repeat the same mistake twice

Highly skilled in CapCut Pro or a comparable editing tool

Strong written and spoken English; able to work independently

Nice-to-Haves

Experience cutting video ads for e-commerce or DTC brands

Experience working directly against Meta or TikTok ad account data

A track record of creatives that scaled on paid

What You'll Learn Here

Most editing jobs teach you software. This one teaches you why video sells.



Direct access to paid performance data on real ad spend, so you see exactly which of your creatives print and which die

1-on-1 mentorship from our Content Lead

Paid courses and software, including the AI video tools you'll be working in

A portfolio backed by numbers, not vibes. "This cut did 4M views and scaled to $X/day" is a career asset that follows you.

Not a Fit If

Your portfolio is mostly long-form, YouTube, or event/wedding content

You can't point to a recent video ad and explain why it performed

You want to make beautiful videos more than videos that sell

You need a fixed schedule or close supervision to stay productive

You're looking for a short-term project or side gig

Working Style

Engagement: Independent contractor, paid in USD

Location: 100% remote

Hours: ~40 hrs/week, long-term role

Schedule: Fully flexible. Work whenever you want, as long as you turn work around quickly and communicate daily (async). No timezone overlap required.

Time off: Flexible PTO. Take the time you need, just coordinate with the team.

Tools: CapCut Pro (or comparable), AI video tools, TikTok/Meta analytics

Working style: No micromanagement

How to Apply

It takes about 5 minutes. We review every application.
